BiblicalUsage: Oniy is affliction, misery, depression, the low state of the oppressed. The Lord hears Hagar's affliction in Genesis 16:11 and names her son Ishmael, and He sees the affliction of His people in Egypt in Exodus 3:7. The bread of affliction is eaten at Passover in Deuteronomy 16:3, and Hannah prays in 1 Samuel 1:11 that the Lord will look on the affliction of His handmaid.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe affliction is the ground where God first shows He hears, because Hagar and Israel and Hannah all find the same Lord listening. My position is that the bread of affliction is the bread of remembrance, and the God who saw it then still sees it now.
